marks.gloss_en: הא לא שהה -- ספיקא הוי: inferred from RSBG's 'whatever lasted thirty days is not a נפל'
hence if he did not last [thirty days], he is a doubt

איני? Rav Huna and Rav Chiyya bar Rav dispute only desecrating Shabbat for the yotze dofen; at eight days we certainly circumcise him -- though his mother is not impure by childbirth (amoraic-memra contradiction; no objection-kind of its own)
הא בהא תליא -- the one depends on the other (= p_ha_beha_talya)
one [of Rav Huna and Rav Chiyya bar Rav]: for one born by caesarean section, or one with two foreskins, one desecrates Shabbat
אלא לתנא קמא ... יליד בית נימול לאחד היכי משכחת לה? -- for the first tanna, how is a home-born circumcised at one found?
R' Yirmeya: [the first tanna's home-born circumcised at one is] one who buys a maidservant for her fetus
הניחא למאן דאמר קנין פירות לאו כקנין הגוף דמי; אלא למאן דאמר קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי, מאי איכא למימר?
בלוקח שפחה על מנת שלא להטבילה -- a replacement case for the second view (= p_mesharshiya_al_menat); see header
Rav Mesharshiya: one who buys a maidservant on condition not to immerse her
[R' Asi's rule] is like [a dispute of] the tannaim
he bought a pregnant maidservant and afterwards she gave birth: that is a purchased [slave] circumcised at eight
he bought a maidservant and she conceived in his possession and gave birth: that is a home-born [slave] circumcised at eight
and the first tanna does not distinguish between immersion before or after the birth: even though his mother is not impure by childbirth, he is circumcised at eight
Rava, per R' Chama: a purchased [slave] circumcised at eight -- where he bought a pregnant maidservant, immersed her, and afterwards she gave birth
RSBG: whatever lasted thirty days, in a human, is not a נפל
